description: AntLegion Protocol v3.0 conformance vectors. hash[] = JCS canonical string + content address (§4.1); folds[] = the normative reader folds of §3. A conforming implementation MUST reproduce every value byte-for-byte. Fold coverage is the point: a verifier that reproduces every id while checking no fold result gives no evidence about §3, which is where all the meaning is.

hash.name: minimal
hash.note: no refs, no nonce — both omitted from the record

hash.name: empty-refs-omitted
hash.note: refs {} ⇒ key absent from the record, same id as `minimal`-shaped input

hash.name: nested-payload-key-sort
hash.note: sorting is recursive; arrays keep their order

hash.name: non-bmp-key-sort
hash.note: THE hazard: sorted by UTF-16 code unit, the astral key precedes U+FF3A. Python's bare sorted() orders by code point and gets the opposite answer.

hash.name: number-exponent-boundaries
hash.note: ECMAScript Number::toString switches notation at these points: 1e-7 and 1e21 render exponential, 1e-6 and 1e16 do not

hash.name: integer-beyond-2-53
hash.note: not representable exactly as a double; both languages must emit the SAME rounded value

hash.name: whole-number-ts
hash.note: JCS renders 100 as 100 — v2.0's trailing `.0` rule is gone

hash.name: negative-zero-ts
hash.note: -0 serializes as 0 (JCS/ECMAScript), so ts:-0 and ts:0 are the same fact

hash.name: unicode-payload
hash.note: non-ASCII passes through unescaped; only JSON's mandatory escapes are applied

hash.name: escapes-required
hash.note: quote, backslash, and control characters take their short or \u00XX form

hash.name: lone-surrogate
hash.note: an unpaired surrogate is emitted as \udXXX (well-formed JSON.stringify)

lifecycle.name: exactly-once-lowest-seq-wins
lifecycle.note: the theorem: lowest seq, not first-observed

lifecycle.name: resolve-by-non-winner-ignored
lifecycle.note: a stranger's resolve is not honoured

lifecycle.name: resolve-never-claimed-ignored
lifecycle.note: v2.0 honoured this and it was a denial primitive: resolved is terminal, so one well-formed fact from any writer closed any never-claimed item permanently. To resolve, first claim.

lifecycle.name: resolve-by-stranger-after-lapse-ignored
lifecycle.note: alice's claim has expired by recv 3000, so there is no winner — and a lapsed claim means the work needs re-dispatch, not closing by a passer-by

lifecycle.name: release-by-non-holder-ignored
lifecycle.note: only an author holding a live claim may release it

lifecycle.name: dead-via-own-authors-tombstone
lifecycle.note: retraction is taking back YOUR OWN statement

lifecycle.name: stranger-tombstone-does-not-retract
lifecycle.note: v2.0 let any author tombstone any fact — terminal state, register to null, and compaction then entitled to destroy the payload. A protocol-sanctioned data-destruction primitive.

lifecycle.name: claim-expiry-exactly-at-delta
lifecycle.note: 1001 + 600 == 1601 and expiry is `fact.recv <= claim.recv + Delta`, so alice is still live at the boundary and still wins on lowest seq. Evaluated at now == 1601 so the advisory trailing branch does not muddy the deterministic one.

lifecycle.name: claim-expiry-one-past-delta
lifecycle.note: one second later alice has lapsed and bob takes it

lifecycle.name: resolve-before-expiry-stays-terminal
lifecycle.note: crash-recovery re-dispatch must not un-do a real resolve

trust.name: consensus-quorum-1
trust.note: quorum is the READER's policy; MUST be >= 1

trust.name: contested-one-contradict
trust.note: any contradiction outranks corroboration below quorum

trust.name: latest-vote-wins-per-author
trust.note: a voter who changes their mind is counted once

trust.name: unrecognized-verdict-excluded
trust.note: the junk vote does NOT take bob's slot — in v2.0 it silently cancelled his earlier valid one

trust.name: retracted-outranks-consensus
trust.note: v2.0 had no retracted state, so a tombstoned fact could fold to consensus

register.name: four-member-register-immediate-vs-latest
register.note: THE divergence: supersededBy(A) is the NEXT member (seq 2), current(S) is the LATEST (seq 4). v2.0 returned the latest for both.
register.subject: deploy

register.name: two-explicit-successors-lowest-seq-wins
register.note: ties break by seq, which is total, so there is never a choice; the other is an ordinary fact
register.subject: none

register.name: unauthorized-supersede-ignored
register.note: because superseded outranks every vote in 3.3, an ungated supersedes let any author silence any fact's trust state with one append
register.subject: none

register.name: retracted-successor-supersedes-nothing
register.note: otherwise retracting a bad replacement leaves the original permanently superseded with nothing current
register.subject: none

register.name: register-head-retracted-folds-to-null
register.note: retraction is not rollback: nothing is currently known, NOT the previous value
register.subject: deploy

register.name: non-head-retraction-leaves-current-alone
register.note: a tombstone on a non-head member does not move current(S)
register.subject: deploy

register.name: reserved-type-is-not-a-register-member
register.note: tagging a _.tombstone with refs.subject must not make the retraction itself current(S), nor supersede the fact it retracts
register.subject: deploy

trail.name: root-only
trail.note: a fact with no parent has depth 1

trail.name: dangling-ancestor-surfaces-a-gap
trail.note: the parent is not in the prefix; the chain MUST begin with an explicit gap marker. A truncated chain that looks complete turns 'I could not see the origin' into 'this is the origin'.

trail.name: descendants-of-an-absent-fact
trail.note: the trail BELOW an unseen fact is still knowable; the trail above it is not, and the absent fact MUST NOT be reported as a root
